subject: Prefetch grace window causing duplicate tokens — request for temporary routing exemption

Subject: Prefetch grace period — duplicate tokens in streaming during POC

Hi Tessa,

Quick note from our engineering lead at VastPay: during our integration POC this morning we saw the streaming model occasionally emit a duplicate prefix (same first 6-12 tokens repeated) when we send long prompt + function-calls. It only happens when the incoming request rate spikes briefly and we have prefetch enabled.

Attached is a small log excerpt (prefetch_log_excerpt.txt) and a short screen grab of the debug trace. We have a demo on Monday and would rather avoid any visible duplicates.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood turn off prefetching or route our tenant to a non-prefetch variant for the demo window?
- If not, any quick mitigation/workaround we can apply client-side?

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Alyssa
Alyssa Turner
Head of Integrations, VastPay

On Thu, Apr 19, 2028 at 09:28 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Forwarding VastPay's report — Alyssa saw duplicate prefix tokens in streaming when request rate spiked. Demo on Monday.

Thanks for the signal, Tessa. Quick read of the log excerpt suggests the symptom matches a known interaction between the prefetch grace window and KV cache eviction when requests from the same session overlap: on heavy concurrency prefetch can occasionally re-issue the initial tokens while the real request is still being reconciled, resulting in duplicates in the outgoing stream.

Short answers:
1) Fastest safe mitigation: route the tenant to the same model binary but with prefetch disabled. That's a config flip on the routing layer; low risk if we scope it to the tenant and limit duration.
2) If we can't flip routing immediately, an alternative is to force client-side idempotency on the first N tokens (client drops exact repeated prefix sequences) — but that's brittle.

Action plan proposal (can do in < 2 hours):
- Create per-tenant routing override (flag: disable-prefetch-for-tenant=DP-4729).
- Apply to VastPay in canary (10% traffic) for first 20 minutes; if no regressions expand to 100%.
- Monitor token-level stream diffs + latency; roll back if tail latency increases >10%.

I'll attach a short playbook for the routing flag and the CLI steps (routing_flag_playbook.md). Need ops to approve the rollout window.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Staff Engineer, Runtime
